palette.$description: Raw values, not meant for components: the CSS uses the roles in `color`. Sampled from screen graphics in frames of a film remake (the bright core of the lit strokes, glow excluded), then moved where legibility needs it: each moved value says so. Frames of the original series are still to be sampled.

void.$description: The monitor glass when nothing is drawn: sampled, the dark of the amber screens

panel.$description: The glass lifted a step, so a panel reads against the page

line.$description: The amber dimmed until frames recede, keeping 3:1

amber.$description: Sampled #e3890d from the text and numbers of the amber monitors, lifted so the signal stands apart from secondary text and from red

amber-dim.$description: The amber dimmed for secondary text, keeping 4.5:1

red.$description: Sampled #f41715 from the alarm hexagons, lifted for legibility: as text it held 4.5:1 on a panel by a hair

panel-alarm.$description: Panel glass under an emergency: the dark of the red screens

red-dim.$description: The red dimmed for frames, keeping 3:1

color.$description: Roles: the only color tokens the CSS uses. A `kanshi.contrast` extension is a promise the tests check: the token's contrast against each `on` token is at least `min` (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.3 for text, 1.4.11 for frames).

accent.$description: The signal color: title tabs, active controls, data lines

on-accent.$description: Text set on an accent fill

on-critical.$description: Text set on a critical fill, such as an alarm hexagon
